title: GPU incident capacity telemetry aggregate 2026-07-11
content:
Purpose
Aggregate telemetry used for the July 11 2026 capacity incident postmortem. This sheet consolidates per-region GPU saturation, queueing backlog, per-cluster throttle events, and sampling of request-level latency/token throughput for impacted time windows. The goal: provide a reproducible set of queries and the key metric slices paired with recommended mitigations.

Incident summary
- Incident id: infra-2026-07-11-capacity-01
- Onset: 2026-07-11T09:18:00Z
- Degraded service window: 09:18:00Z - 10:47:00Z (visibility up to 11:30Z for slow drains)
- Primary effect: elevated request queueing and region-level throttles that increased tail latency and caused ~12% request failures for hosted API tier.
- Affected regions: us-west1 (primary), eu-west1 (spillover), ap-southeast1 (minor).
- Primary hardware families: A100-40GB and H100-80GB pools with mixed preemptible burst capacity.

Top-level findings (quick list)
1) Progressive saturation in us-west1 GPU pool due to an unexpected traffic spike from a single large customer job (identified by request-tag client: ACME_DOCS_BATCH).
2) Autoscaler reaction lag (policy min-cooldown 6m) and reservation fragmentation prevented timely allocation of burst capacity.
3) Continuous batching increased effective concurrency and caused KV cache pressure, which amplified per-request token generation time on long sequences (>2k tokens).
4) Global routing fallback kicked in but resulted in throttles on eu-west1 because the fallback capacity had separate per-customer reservations leading to quota exhaustion.

Sampling methodology
- Primary telemetry sources: per-request logs (logging pipeline), GPU utilization (prometheus -> longterm metrics), scheduler events (k8s events), autoscaler traces, per-region throttle logs.
- Time windows captured: pre-incident baseline (2026-07-11T08:00:00Z - 09:17:59Z), incident window (09:18:00Z - 10:47:00Z), recovery tail (10:48:00Z - 11:30:00Z).
- Sampling constraints: for per-request traces we sampled 10% uniformly and forced-included any trace with tag client:ACME_DOCS_BATCH or error:true.
- Consistency note: token throughput derived from model-side counters; there is known ~1–2% jitter due to aggregation latency across hosts.

Key metric slices (CSV rows follow)
Columns: time_window, region, gpu_family, avg_gpu_util_pct, p95_request_queue_ms, queued_requests_peak, throttle_event_count, failed_requests_pct, avg_tokens_per_request
Rows:
"2026-07-11T08:00-09:17","us-west1","A100-40GB","38","15","12","0","0.8","210"
"2026-07-11T09:18-10:47","us-west1","A100-40GB","89","420","148","37","12.3","1860"
"2026-07-11T09:18-10:47","eu-west1","H100-80GB","67","210","62","21","5.6","920"
"2026-07-11T09:18-10:47","ap-southeast1","A100-40GB","52","90","18","2","1.2","540"
"2026-07-11T10:48-11:30","us-west1","A100-40GB","56","68","34","4","2.1","980"

Representative per-request anomaly samples (n=6)
- trace_id: t-93ba, client:ACME_DOCS_BATCH, region:us-west1, queued_ms:612, model:rwkv-13b, tokens:3200, result:error (timeout)
- trace_id: t-93bd, client:internal-loadtest, region:us-west1, queued_ms:402, model:gptx-lite, tokens:120, result:ok (latency 2.1s)
- trace_id: t-93c1, client:ACME_DOCS_BATCH, region:eu-west1 (fallback), queued_ms:512, model:rwkv-13b, tokens:2800, result:throttled
- trace_id: t-93c6, client:svc-search, region:ap-southeast1, queued_ms:88, model:embedder-2x, tokens:64, result:ok
- trace_id: t-93d0, client:ACME_DOCS_BATCH, region:us-west1, queued_ms:714, model:rwkv-13b, tokens:4000, result:error (evicted)
- trace_id: t-93d7, client:unknown, region:us-west1, queued_ms:390, model:gptx-lite, tokens:512, result:ok

SQL queries used (BigQuery) - copy/paste-ready
1) Region-level GPU utilization aggregation
SELECT region, gpu_family, TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(event_time, MINUTE) as minute, AVG(gpu_util_pct) as avg_gpu_util_pct, PERCENTILE_CONT(queue_ms, 0.95) as p95_queue_ms, SUM(queued_count) as queued_requests_peak
FROM `redwood-telemetry.cluster_gpu_metrics`
WHERE event_time BETWEEN "2026-07-11T08:00:00Z" AND "2026-07-11T11:30:00Z"
GROUP BY region, gpu_family, minute
ORDER BY minute

2) Throttle event rollup by region and cause
SELECT region, throttle_cause, COUNT(1) as throttle_event_count
FROM `redwood-telemetry.throttle_events`
WHERE event_time BETWEEN "2026-07-11T09:00:00Z" AND "2026-07-11T11:30:00Z"
GROUP BY region, throttle_cause
ORDER BY throttle_event_count DESC

3) Per-request sample joins (forced includes + 10% sample)
SELECT r.trace_id, r.client_id, r.region, r.queued_ms, r.model, r.tokens, r.result, s.gpu_host, s.gpu_util_pct, s.kv_cache_miss_pct
FROM `redwood-telemetry.request_traces` r
LEFT JOIN `redwood-telemetry.host_metrics` s ON r.host_id = s.host_id AND TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(r.request_time, MINUTE) = TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(s.event_time, MINUTE)
WHERE r.request_time BETWEEN "2026-07-11T09:18:00Z" AND "2026-07-11T10:47:00Z"
AND (r.force_included=true OR r.sample_fraction=0.10)
LIMIT 1000

Immediate mitigations taken during incident
- Manually bumped autoscaler aggressiveness for us-west1 (reduced cooldown to 90s) at 09:35Z; partial relief by 09:54Z.
- Temporarily increased per-customer fallback quota in eu-west1 for ACME_DOCS_BATCH to allow graceful spillover at 09:44Z.
- Deployed KV cache eviction tuning (reduce cache retention for long-run jobs) at 09:58Z which improved model-side token throughput by ~12% on sampled hosts.

Root causes (hypothesized, validated where noted)
- Primary: a large batched job from ACME_DOCS_BATCH submitted as high-concurrency continuous-batching requests with long sequences (>2k tokens) that were not covered by existing cost/burst protection rules. (validated via request tags and billing plan correlation)
- Secondary: autoscaler config tuned for cost-smoothing (long cooldown) which slowed capacity ramp. (validated by comparing scale events to policy)
- Tertiary: per-region fallback quotas are per-customer and not shared with global fallback pool; this caused eu-west1 to throttle spilled requests. (validated via throttle logs)

Recommendations (short-term)
- Add a per-client concurrent-job limit enforcement in the routing tier for continuous-batch style requests. Assign enforcement priority to avoid single-customer saturation.
- Temporarily relax autoscaler cooldown for high-priority regions during detected saturation spikes (policy toggle). Implement an automated detector to lower cooldown on >75% sustained GPU util for 3 minutes.
- Create a global fallback quota pool that can be used when regional reservations are exhausted; have a fast-path reallocation logic.
- Introduce a preflight check to block super-long sequence continuous-batch jobs from entering hosted API without explicit reservation/commit. Return 429 with guidance.

Recommendations (longer-term)
- Rework autoscaler to consider request queue depth and model sequence length distribution (not only GPU util) when deciding scale actions.
- Improve continuous-batch isolation: identify and optionally isolate high-token workloads into dedicated pools with stricter admission control.
- Post-incident capacity simulation: run synthetic ACME_DOCS_BATCH traffic across staging clusters with current autoscaler config to validate mitigations and tune thresholds.

Action items and owners
- Implement routing-level per-client concurrency limiter (owner: Ravi Menon) - due 2026-07-22
- Create autoscaler policy toggle and detector (owner: Sofia Alvarez) - due 2026-07-20
- Design global fallback quota prototype (owner: Ethan Park) - discovery complete by 2026-07-25
- Add preflight job size check and user-facing guidance path (owner: Product: Nikhil Rao) - 2026-07-29

Notes for postmortem writeup
- Use the aggregated CSV rows above as the canonical metric table in the postmortem; include links to the raw BigQuery exports to keep provenance.
- Capture customer communication timeline for ACME (CS leads) and attach to Confluence postmortem.
- Validate billing attribution for ACME_DOCS_BATCH to determine whether rate-limiting or surcharge is the right remedial tool.

Appendix: quick diagnostic commands
- Prometheus query for p95 queue: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_queue_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le, region))
- kubectl: kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --selector=pool=us-west1-a100
- Autoscaler events: gcloud logging read 'resource.type=k8s_cluster AND labels.autoscaler=true' --start-time="2026-07-11T09:00:00Z" --end-time="2026-07-11T11:30:00Z"

End of sheet. Attach this JSON to the postmortem folder and link the BigQuery exports.
